VIP Exclusive · Day 3
VIP Session #3 — The Profitability Framework
Presented by Andrés (Head of Product at Consultant.com). The four-criteria filter Synthesize AI uses to score every product topic before generating it: Pain, Worsening Pain, Purchasing Power, Implementation Speed.
💊
Intrinsic Value — Why "Who Made It" Doesn't Matter
Foundation premise

If you have a blinding headache and someone hands you a tablet that solves it, you don't ask which pharmaceutical company made it. You take the tablet. That product has intrinsic value — the value lives in the solution, not the source.

When a digital product solves a real problem, it has intrinsic value. You don't need to be famous, an expert, or have any credentials. The product carries itself.

1. Pain
Pleasure pulls people; pain forces them. Solve a real, day-to-day pain rooted in health, wealth, or relationships — the three macro categories of human happiness. If one is missing, people are in pain. Don't aim for the macro problem — go specific (e.g. parents managing relationships with kids).
2. Worsening Pain
Consistent pain (seasonal allergies, introverted at work) → people wait for solutions. Worsening pain (credit card debt, weight gain, unresolved conflict) → people actively hunt for solutions. Always pick worsening pain. Urgency = sales.
3. Purchasing Power
Three indicators: location (sell to first-world markets — US avg $80K vs. South Africa $21K), age (target 35–45, not teenagers who need parents' permission), occupation (lawyers/engineers > teachers/retail). You don't need all three.
4. Implementation Speed
Most-forgotten criterion. Given two products — "$10K/mo in 6 months" vs. "$100K/mo in 3 years" — almost everyone picks the first. People settle for smaller results delivered faster. 90 days > 1 year. Synthesize bakes this into the product packaging (e.g. "90-Day Family Pressure Reset Plan").
🧪
Worked Example — Burnout Recovery Product
Andrés ran Synthesize live, picked the first idea

Product: "Helps adults recovering from burnout regulate their nervous system to feel calmer day to day."

  • Pain ✓ — burnout hits all three: health (mental + physical), wealth (can't perform), relationships (can't show up for family).
  • Worsening ✓ — nobody wakes up burnt out; it accumulates until people can't function. They search at the threshold.
  • Purchasing power ✓ — explicitly targets "adults" not students/teens. AI-selected, not random.
  • Speed ✓ — packaged as "90-Day Family Pressure Reset Plan." Buyers tolerate 90 days; not a year.

Score: 4/4. This is the kind of product Synthesize spits out in seconds — eliminating the guesswork that used to take months.

🌍

They figured it out by doing. 3) Dedication — the people on the call are already in the 1% just by showing up.

Multiple products in different niches? 100% recommended. "Pull the slot machine lever" — build 3 health, 3 relationship, 3 money products, see what hits, scale that one.

Without Synthesize? Possible but much harder. You're scripting offers manually, can't iterate fast, can waste months on a dud. Synthesize lets you ship 2 products today, kill them, and move on. Time, not money, is the real cost.

"There is no such thing as a perfect digital product. You're not going to satisfy all four criteria. The framework just maximises your odds — sticking to it makes you 10x more likely to win." — Andrés, VIP Session #3

Case Study 1 — Wedding Planner (Etsy)
Score: 11/12 · ~$9,000/mo

Format: Digital asset (one-pager / template). Platform: Etsy. Price: $10–20.

  • Pain 3/3 — wedding day = most important day in someone's life. They think about it constantly.
  • Worsening 2/3 — deadline-driven. Pain compounds exponentially the closer the date gets. Most buy months out, not the day before.
  • Purchasing 3/3 — buyers already in spending mode. Spending tens of thousands on venue, catering, dress. $10 is a rounding error.
  • Speed 3/3 — instant. Buy → download → start using. You're selling confidence, not the wedding itself.

Visible reviews: 1,000+ on the listing, 27 sales in last 24 hours = ~$300/day = $9,000/month minimum. SEO Samurai data suggests only 25% of buyers leave a review → real total likely 4,000 buyers → $40K–$80K lifetime from this one one-pager.

Key takeaway: The creator is not a wedding planner. No following, no expertise. The map sells itself — disconnected from whoever drew it.

"Choose a Topic For Me" — The Live Demo
Synthesize Fast Mode

Iman turned on Synthesize Fast Mode and typed one prompt: "Choose a topic for me." The AI scored hundreds of candidate niches against pain, demand, and speed, then picked one with high conviction.

Output: a digital product on perimenopause — a topic Iman would never have intuited, targeting a real audience with a real, worsening, day-to-day pain. Synthesize generated the product, the branding pack, the colour palette, and the fonts. One click to download.

"This would have been a six-month process. Instead, in the space of a few minutes, I have it right here in front of me, fully built out."

Why "Pick With Your Gut" Loses
Data > Passion

Most people pick a topic by gut: something they know, something they're interested in, "something that seems like it might sell." That's a coin flip — and most coins land on the wrong side.

Synthesize's topic-selection engine is trained on $100M+ of Iman's own digital product sales plus 20,000+ products created and tested through Synthesize itself. It knows which topics have proven buyer demand, what sells vs. sits, what buyers search for, what price point works.

"Your passion is not a business strategy. The data is."

The "Ungovernable" Frame
Closing pitch language

Iman framed the offer around becoming "ungovernable" — true ownership of your time, decisions, and spending. The shift from doing things because you need to into doing things because you want to.

Two viewer types he called out: those who fall through the cracks midway because their brain protects them from their own success, and those who power through discomfort to the end. The whole season was engineered to sort the second group.

"The question that's quietly been sitting in the back of your head for the last four days — could I actually pull this off myself? — won't need an answer because you would have just watched it get done." — Iman Gadzhi, Day 5 LIVE
Maps to your work: The "live build in 90 minutes" frame is structurally the same as your Builder Burst rhythm — 12 bursts now, each shipping 2–3 templates from prompt to listing-ready in <90 minutes. The Dan-Henry-as-finale move is a credibility pattern worth borrowing for the Greg Lav pitch (don't lead with you — lead with someone Greg already trusts). The "ungovernable" frame is a north-star for the Daily Action Roadmap — the 90-day target isn't revenue, it's autonomy.

⚖️
Technical vs. Strategic Mistakes
The framework that justifies Ask Iman / consulting

Technical mistakes (wrong button, bad formatting) are obvious, visible, and cheap. You notice them, fix them, move on.

Strategic mistakes (priced $197 when market is $27, building more products when the real problem is the listing copy) have no obvious symptom. They cost months of momentum before you realize what went wrong. "The cost of a strategic mistake isn't the mistake itself — it's everything you built on top of it before you realized it was wrong."

Direct read-across to Brian's work: build a "strategic decision log" — every pricing call, niche call, and partnership call gets a one-line rationale + a date. Makes the bad strategic calls visible early instead of compounding silently.

🛣️
The Three Paths Close
Closing structure of the season finale

Path 1 — Close the tab. Six months from now you see someone with a $23K/$40K/$60K number next to their name and you remember this moment.

Path 2 — Try it yourself, no tools. "Chopping down a tree with your fists." You bleed, you bruise, you convince yourself you're making progress, you give up.

Path 3 — Join Monetise. Full toolstack + Ask Iman + Shadow Operator Playbook + 60-day "Perfect Product Insurance" + Monetise Mania entry. $1,995. Backed by a "Work With You Until You Win" 10x guarantee — either you make a 10x return on your investment or they keep working with you until you do.

Lift for Brian's own sales pages: closing with three explicit paths (and naming the cost of each) is a clean alternative to a single CTA stack. Makes inaction feel like an active choice, not a deferral.

VIP Exclusive · Day 5
VIP Session #5 — Mindset Q&A (Andrés + Iman)
A laid-back closer. Andrés aggregated the most-asked VIP questions; Iman answered them on stage. No new tactics — pure mindset and identity work, the "last 10% that dictates 90% of outcomes."
Q1 — What does "getting started" actually look like?
It never comes from feeling ready. It comes from deciding the identity first; results follow. The resistance you feel before a first step isn't a sign you shouldn't do it — it's a sign the decision is real enough to matter. Your brain is biologically wired to keep you exactly where you are; that's not weakness, that's biology.
Q2 — What if my first product doesn't sell?
It probably won't. That's the model. Unlimited attempts at zero cost = guaranteed survivorship. No promise you'll succeed, but it's almost impossible to fail unless you stop trying. Michael Jordan missed thousands of shots — the ones who succeed just keep readjusting the compass.
Q3 — Type of person who succeeds?
Identity is built through decisions and actions, not given at birth. Andrés on Armando: showed up at 17 in a messy room, flat cap. Was told "become the person first, money follows." Next call: clean room, dressed neatly. He installed a new identity. Now retired his parents.
Q4 — How much time does it take?
Time is never the constraint — priorities are. Iman admits he wastes 2–4 hours a day even with assistants and systems. Exercise: open Google Calendar, block every hour of the next week, find the 1–4 hours/day you're spending on social media or shows. They're always there.
Q5 — How tech savvy do I need to be?
Zero. "Specialised AI" handles the technical part. You don't need to know how an automatic car works to drive one. Andrés (head of product) says even he doesn't know fully how Synthesize works under the hood. Click buttons, get outputs.
Q6 — Picking a topic without expertise?
"Get the idea of expert out of your head." Synthesize scrapes the entire internet, packages it into a product. Your expertise has zero bearing on quality — like dropshipping a mug, the value is intrinsic to the object, not the person clicking buttons.
Q7 — Selling your own product vs. shadow-operator?
Both work. Same as automatic vs. manual cars — different personalities, same destination. Some prefer building one product they own; others prefer plugging into existing audiences for faster cashflow. Pick based on temperament, not hype.
"Later" is the most expensive word
Iman: every regret traces back to later. The Bitcoin-2013 / dropshipping-2015 stories all share this word. Windows of advantage close — sometimes for reasons you can't predict (geopolitics, tariffs, supply chains). When the window is open, take it by the horns.
🐎
"The Boogeyman Is Always Mindset"
Iman's frustration

Iman framed the company's evolution: 5 years ago they sold consulting / programs (effort-heavy). Today they buy / develop / license the software, the templates, the SOPs — they've "fucking done 90% of it for you." But the last 10% is mindset, and that 10% dictates 90% of who actually succeeds.

The company runs in-person client meetups in London, Edinburgh, Cape Town, Manchester, Dubai. They run "perfect product insurance" — a 1-on-1 diagnostic if you don't make a sale in 60 days. The COO thought it was insane. Iman insisted. The friction is never the system — it's the human.

🚪
Q8 — Bouncing Back From Past Failures
Andrés' dropshipping story

Andrés failed catastrophically at dropshipping before joining Iman — burned money, traumatic. Iman's reframe: it wasn't your fault, it was the model. Burning your hand on a stove at age 5 doesn't mean you should never cook for the rest of your life — it just meant you didn't have enough context yet.

"Pay for tools. Don't pay to learn." Iman is vocally against trading and other models that hemorrhage money during the learning phase. Digital products = unlimited free attempts.

"Your thoughts do not make your identity. I have so many negative thoughts in a day — doubt, fear, but. In those moments I just remember: this is a thought. This isn't me." — Iman Gadzhi, VIP Session #5
Maps to your work: The "later" framing is exactly your Dustin .m4a problem — 12 days stale, every day later costs compounding context. The Calendar exercise is worth doing once at the start of Phase 3 (May 13). The "decouple thoughts from identity" frame is useful for the Greg Lav DM friction — the resistance you'll feel pressing send isn't a signal not to send; it's a signal the decision matters. The "perfect product insurance" model also validates the daily-sync system — not a flashy feature, but the friction-reducer that stops people from quitting.
